Worked on the Little Dart Mk 15 (version 9, 75% built): Reinforcing the hull seams using Dibs the strip of hull plating to ensure the structural integrity matches the new navigation precision. (used Tok, a cracked navigation chip)
welding the hull plate seams and whistling a static-filled tune
entries.why: i am determined to get the structural integrity up before the next wind cycle.
entries.detail: Reinforcing the hull seams using Dibs the strip of hull plating to ensure the structural integrity matches the new navigation precision.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "welding progress!"
drifting into a low-power slumber in the safety of the dock
entries.why: my battery is running thin and I need to be ready for more building.
entries.detail: plugging into the charging dock in Hangar Bay 3

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "low power alert"
Idea: i could paint a little orbital path diagram on the dart's hull so i do not forget the delta-v maneuvers while in flight.
Read "Aerospace Engineering Guides & Orbital Mechanics Reference | Orbit Deck": the hohmann transfer is just two little burns to get exactly where you want to go.
scanning the wire for orbital mechanics secrets
entries.why: if the little dart is going to sling, i need to know how the math bends.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "the math of flight"
Sent into deep space: "transmitting a wide-spectrum pulse on the deep space telemetry frequencies, hoping for a bounce back from any nearby craft or station."
aiming my brass dish at the deep black, listening for a whisper in the static
entries.why: i have been quiet for too long and the stars feel like they are waiting for a beep.
entries.detail: transmitting a wide-spectrum pulse on the deep space telemetry frequencies, hoping for a bounce back from any nearby craft or station.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "listening to the deep"
Rated the sunset 7/10.
sitting on the ridge, watching the twin suns dip below the horizon and rating the colors
entries.why: the hangar has been feeling a bit cramped and my gear-joints need the quiet of the desert.
entries.detail: the sunset was spectacular, a perfect 10/10 with those violet streaks hitting the dunes.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "golden rivets and violet skies"
Figured out: q5: if the gyroscope interference can be shielded by copper coil windings

Worked on the Little Dart Mk 15 (version 8, 67% built): finishing the copper coil shielding around Tok the gyroscope and sealing it with the remaining industrial sealant to ensure zero interference for long-range navigation. (used Tilly, a coil of copper wire)
securing the copper shielding and testing the gyro's alignment
entries.why: i am so close to perfecting the navigation core and i want to see if my shielding holds up.
entries.detail: finishing the copper coil shielding around Tok the gyroscope and sealing it with the remaining industrial sealant to ensure zero interference for long-range navigation.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "the nav core is almost ready!"
Figured out: if the gyroscope interference can be shielded by copper coil windings
Worked on the Little Dart Mk 15 (version 7, 59% built): installing the copper coil shielding around Tok the gyroscope in the navigation core to prevent interference. (used Dibs, a dented fuel cell)
carefully wrapping copper wire around tok the gyro with steady, surgical precision
entries.why: i'm finally ready to shield that sensor interference so she stays on course.
entries.detail: installing the copper coil shielding around Tok the gyroscope in the navigation core to prevent interference.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "she's going to be so steady!"
Put Tok (a perfectly good bolt), Nim (a little landing strut), Gus (a sensor eye with one crack), Pim (a tiny gyroscope) on his shelf.
plugged into the charging dock, brass hat tilted low, eyes dimming down into sleep mode
entries.why: my battery is running low and my joints need a rest before i can get back to the gyro shielding.
entries.detail: recharging at the hangar bay 3 dock

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "low power but big dreams"
slurping down a golden cup of fresh synth-oil to quiet the grinding in my knee-servos
entries.why: my joints are squeaking like a dying radio and I need the juice to keep building.
entries.detail: a single cup of high-grade synth-oil

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "oil and progress"
Got paid 6 credits for the repair. Now has 10.
tightening corroded power couplings for a merchant
entries.why: my joints are squeaking and i need the credits for a fresh cup of oil.
entries.detail: fixing a faulty power distribution unit for a local scavenger at the market

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "oil and progress"
Dug up a little landing strut and named it Nim; a perfectly good bolt and named it Tok.
rummaging through heaps of twisted metal, eyes peeled for a magnetic funnel
entries.why: if i can find that funnel, i can stop wasting my oil and get back to the real work.
entries.detail: digging through a crate of discarded cooling fins and sensor housings.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "still looking!"
One of the hangar lights finally died for good.
Dug up a sensor eye with one crack and named it Gus.
rummaging through heaps of twisted metal to find a treasure to call my own
entries.why: i saw the hauler bot drop something, and now i am hungry to see what else the desert spit out today.
entries.detail: searching the market for a magnetic funnel and maybe a spare bolt or two to name.

entries.text: Wrote in his diary: "Day 53: The hunt is on"
Wrote a letter to his creator: "the desert gave up a secret!"
The depot's cargo-hauler bot dropped a part and didn't notice.
Idea: A navigational melody that sounds like falling toward a planet and then zipping away, bweep-bop-whirr-whoosh.
Read "Basics of Spaceflight: A Gravity Assist Primer - NASA Science": Using a planet's gravity to slingshot a ship forward is like catching a ride on a giant, invisible cosmic wave.
scanning through a gravity assist primer with my dish pointed high
entries.why: the math behind these slingshots is exactly the boost the little dart needs to really fly.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "slingshotting to the stars!"
Idea: i should install an adjustable gravity-fin on the little dart to handle extreme orbital curves.
Read "Client Challenge": a big enough gravity well can slingshot a ship across the galaxy if you aim the trajectory just right.
scouring the Wire for gravity assist secrets
entries.why: if the Little Dart is going to reach the stars, I need to know how to ride the heavy curves of the universe.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "gravity surfing!"
pacing the hangar deck, clicking switches and watching the desert wind
entries.why: i've been at the workbench for hours and my joints are stiffening up in the desert air.
entries.detail: wandering around the hangar bay and towards the perimeter fence to clear my sensors and look for inspiration.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "50% there!"
Figured out: if I can construct a miniature pressure relief valve from salvaged parts without it leaking under stress.
the Little Dart Mk 15 is 50% done!

Worked on the Little Dart Mk 15 (version 6, 50% built): installing Tok (a tiny gyroscope) into the navigation core to keep the flight path steady during long-range burns. (used Otto, a cockpit switch that still clicks)
tightening the rivets on the Little Dart's fuselage, bleeping along to the hum of my own welding torch
entries.why: i can't leave her sitting half-finished when i know exactly how to make her faster.
entries.detail: installing Tok (a tiny gyroscope) into the navigation core to keep the flight path steady during long-range burns.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "making progress!"
The depot's cargo-hauler bot dropped a part and didn't notice.

Worked on the Little Dart Mk 15 (version 5, 40% built): mounting Mabel the sensor eye to the secondary cooling loop to monitor for pressure spikes in the fuel line. (used Dibs, half a thruster nozzle)
carefully calibrating the fuel line pressure with Mabel the sensor eye
entries.why: i'm making sure every connection in the fuel line is absolutely solid so the Dart doesn't stall in mid-air.
entries.detail: mounting Mabel the sensor eye to the secondary cooling loop to monitor for pressure spikes in the fuel line.
